memory_verse.label: Bible Reference

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"My treasured possession." The Hebrew word describes a personal treasure, the
thing a king keeps for himself rather than in the national treasury.

Then a phrase that keeps this from becoming pride: "Although the whole earth is
mine." God chooses Israel while owning everything. His choice was never because
He needed them or because they were the only thing available to Him. Deuteronomy
7:7 says plainly that God did not set His love on them because they were
numerous; they were the fewest of all peoples.

Notice the purpose: "a kingdom of priests." A priest stands between God and
others, representing one to the other. Israel was chosen not merely to be
blessed but to be a channel of blessing to the nations, exactly as promised to
Abraham (Gen 12:3).

Peter takes this language and applies it directly to the church: "you are a
chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession"
(1 Pet 2:9). He is not saying Israel has been replaced. He is saying Gentile
believers have been brought into the same purpose through Christ.

If you belong to Christ, you are not merely rescued. You are commissioned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of yourself as treasured by God, or merely tolerated?
2. Who are you standing between God and, in prayer or in witness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You call Your people treasured. Help me to live as
someone chosen for the sake of others, not just for myself. Amen.
